newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares jump 2.53 pct to new record.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares jump 2.53 pct to new record.

text.p: Istanbul shares leapt an average 2.53 percent amid selective buys on Thursday to resume the market's string of records after Wednesday's 1.29 percent downward correction, brokers said.
The IMKB-100 closed 2,320.38 points higher at 93,923.04, compared to Tuesday's previous all-time high closing of 92,797.71. It surged to a high of 94,574 in the afternoon from an early low of 91,475.
Trade volume eased to 15.97 trillion lira from 16.17 trillion on Wednesday.
The index had gained 1.13 percent in the first two days of this week after last week's 5.49 percent surge, totalling seven consecutive daily records.
In dollar terms, the index stood at $0.9 compared to a record of $1 on April 8 and $0.67 at end-1995.
Brokers said the market pierced resistance at the index's 93,000 level and tested 94,500, but weak volume caused activity to remain highly selective.
"Trade was quite lively and on the buying side today in contrast to yesterday. But this activity is not yet supported by an increase in volume," said Nazmi Sarikaya from Disbank.
"The index seems to have settled in the 90,000-95,000 range but better volume and stronger activity in locomotive (bluechip) shares are needed to overcome 95,000," he added.
Brokers said selective demand was based on end-1996 profit prospects of companies.

Of the 227 shares traded, gainers outdid losers sharply by 134 to 30 and 63 closed steady. The 85-share industrial index rose 1.53 percent to 99,093.98 and the 15-share financial index surged 4.81 percent to 91,185.99.

Actives were led by utility Aktas Elektrik, up 1,000 lira at 92,000, foreign trade firm EGS Dis Ticaret, up 1,500 lira at 18,000 and car and commercial vehicle maker Otosan, up 4,500 lira at 46,500. Together, they made up 20.9 percent of the total volume.
